About World Vision Iraq World Vision Iraq (WV Iraq) has operated since 2014 across Erbil, Kirkuk, Ninewa, Salah al‑Din, Anbar, and Thi‑Qar, partnering with government, local NGOs, and the private sector to reduce climate and disaster risks and protect children and vulnerable households. noticias.contenido: Country: Iraq Source: World Vision Please refer to the attached file. About World Vision Iraq World Vision Iraq (WV Iraq) has operated since 2014 across Erbil, Kirkuk, Ninewa, Salah al‑Din, Anbar, and Thi‑Qar, partnering with government, local NGOs, and the private sector to reduce climate and disaster risks and protect children and vulnerable households. We combine disaster risk reduction (DRR), climate adaptation, water security, and resilient livelihoods to deliver sustainable results in fragile settings. Context Iraq is among the countries most vulnerable to climate change. Its geographical location makes it particularly susceptible to various hydrological, meteorological, and climatological risks due to its arid climate and downstream position. In recent years, Iraq has recorded its lowest rainfall in two decades, leading to water scarcity, below-average vegetation growth, and reduced crop yields. These challenges worsen existing vulnerabilities, especially among marginalized communities. Our approaches The primary objective of WV Iraqʼs Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Resilience programming is to strengthen community resilience against disasters and ensure a safer environment for children by addressing the underlying drivers of risk and vulnerability in a changing climate. WV Iraq has a strong track record in disaster risk management and anticipatory action. Our expertise includes: Risk Assessment and Early Warning Systems We conduct climate and disaster risk analyses Capacity Statement to produce community risk maps and establish practical early warning protocols with clear activation triggers for anticipatory actions such as inputs, and asset protection. Scenario‑based plans and crisis modifiers enable fast, adaptive responses across humanitarian, development, and peace programmes. Community-Based Disaster Risk Management (CBDRM) We prioritize building the capacity of vulnerable communities to prepare for and respond to disasters. This includes training community members on disaster preparedness, establishing community-based disaster management committees, and conducting drills and simulations. Resilient livelihoods We promote climate-resilient livelihoods through CSA practices, including Farmer Field Schools, conservation agriculture, efficient irrigation, and improved seed and soil management. Financial resilience is supported through S4T groups and financial literacy, complemented by private-sector partnerships that expand access to inputs and services. Integrated water resources management We promote sustainable water management by implementing multiple-use water systems that serve domestic needs, agriculture, livestock, and livelihoods, ensuring equitable access and long-term resource protection. We also strengthen WASH committees by training them to manage water and sanitation services safely and efficiently, engage communities, and uphold environmental safeguards.

noticias.contenido: Country: Iraq Source: World Vision Please refer to the attached file. COP31 - ANTALYA, TÜRKIYE - 9 - 20 NOVEMBER 2026 CONTEXT AND NEED: Iraq is among the countries most severely impacted by climate change, experiencing significant water scarcity, and rapid desertification, leading to the annual loss of 60,000 acres of arable land. The country faces soaring temperatures, diminishing rainfall, intensified droughts, frequent sand and dust storms, and periodic flooding. These issues are exacerbated by rapid population growth, urbanization, and regional political instability, which impede effective water management and sustainable development. Consequently, there is a growing crisis of climate-induced migration, with more than 186,000 already displaced. Urgent, coordinated action from the Iraqi government, international actors, and local communities is required to mitigate impacts, enhance resilience, and address these multifaceted threats.

noticias.titulo: Photon fluctuations offer new way to probe electron dynamics in crystals
noticias.resumen: Intense laser light can make a crystal emit new colors at frequencies many times higher than that of the original beam. This process, known as high-harmonic generation, provides a powerful way to investigate the rapid motion of electrons in solids. Researchers usually study the brightness and spectrum of the emitted light. Yet those measurements capture only part of the available information. Fluctuations between individual laser pulses can also reveal how the emission is produced.

noticias.contenido: Country: Afghanistan Source: World Bank Please refer to the attached file. Strong Harvest Lifts Afghanistan’s Economy, but Falling Incomes and Water Shortages Strain Families KABUL, November 18, 2026 — Afghanistan’s economy is expected to grow by 3 percent in 2026, driven almost entirely by a strong harvest. However, output per person is set to fall by 3.3 percent, its third consecutive annual decline, as the population is projected to grow by 6.6 percent, according to the World Bank’s latest Afghanistan Development Update . The Fall 2026 report, which includes a special focus on water security, finds that many families are under pressure, while the country’s water reserves are shrinking. Fewer workdays and higher food prices have reduced what families can afford. In September 2026, casual laborers found 14 percent fewer days of work than a year earlier, while their weekly earnings bought 27 percent less wheat flour. And despite the improved harvest, an estimated 15.9 million people faced acute food insecurity in September and October 2026, according to the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC). Domestic revenue rose by 10.2 percent in the first half of 2026 as domestic taxes and non-tax revenue offset a fall in customs duties. Public investment remains low, with capital spending projected at about 1.3 percent of GDP for the fiscal year. With the border with Pakistan closed, about 97 percent of Afghanistan’s imports now enter through Central Asia and Iran. Exports fell by 15.1 percent in April–September 2026 compared with the same period a year earlier. The report also finds that Afghanistan has lost an estimated 4.9 billion cubic meters of freshwater reserves a year since 2003. In Kabul, groundwater is being drawn nearly four times as fast as it is naturally replenished. Water shortages are also putting rural livelihoods at risk. Agriculture accounts for 46 percent of employment and 95 percent of water withdrawals. Looking ahead, economic growth is projected to reach 3.3 percent in 2027 and 3.5 percent in 2028. Even under this projected recovery, output per person in 2028 is expected to remain about 7 percent below its 2024 level. A poor harvest, further disruptions to trade routes, additional large-scale returns, or deeper aid cuts could weaken the outlook. The report identifies more reliable trade routes, expanded employment in provinces receiving large numbers of returnees, and restored access to education and work for women and girls as priorities for improving living standards. On water, it calls for restoring essential water and sanitation services, repairing irrigation systems, and protecting watersheds and groundwater reserves. About the Afghanistan Development Update: The Afghanistan Development Update is part of the World Bank’s ongoing research, monitoring, and analytical work on Afghanistan’s economy and society. It aims to support evidence-based policymaking and inform the international community on economic developments in Afghanistan. Contacts In Kabul Payamulhaq Barrai pbarrai@worldbankgroup.org In Washington Serene Jweied sjweied@worldbankgroup.org

noticias.resumen: Country: Ukraine Source: European Commission Please refer to the attached file. €237.6 billion in overall support to Ukraine and Ukrainians including €3.8 billion from the proceeds of Russian immobilised assets The EU stands united in its unwavering support for Ukraine in the face of Russia’s war of aggression and its illegal attempts to annex Ukrainian territory. The EU continues to work relentlessly with international partners to make sure Ukraine receives the material support it needs and to hold Russia accountable for its actions. The EU has also offered temporary protection to over four…
noticias.contenido: Country: Ukraine Source: European Commission Please refer to the attached file. €237.6 billion in overall support to Ukraine and Ukrainians including €3.8 billion from the proceeds of Russian immobilised assets The EU stands united in its unwavering support for Ukraine in the face of Russia’s war of aggression and its illegal attempts to annex Ukrainian territory. The EU continues to work relentlessly with international partners to make sure Ukraine receives the material support it needs and to hold Russia accountable for its actions. The EU has also offered temporary protection to over four million people fleeing the war and is committed to continue providing strong political, financial, economic, humanitarian, military and diplomatic support to Ukraine and its people for as long as it takes . The EU opened accession negotiations with Ukraine. SUPPORT FOR UKRAINE’S ECONOMY The EU has established the Ukraine Facility of up to €50 billion to provide predictable and flexible support to Ukraine for the period 2024-2027 to support recovery, reconstruction and modernisation, in line with its EU path. So far, a total amount of more than €31.4 billion of direct assistance to Ukraine has been provided (excluding external contributions). The total EU commitments under the Ukraine Investment Framework now reach €8.5 billion , expecting to leverage over €25.7 billion in investments. The EU set up a €90 billion Ukraine Support Loan for 2026 and 2027 , based on EU borrowing on the capital markets backed by the EU budget headroom. Two thirds are indicatively dedicated to defence procurement support, and one third to overall budgetary assistance. €25.8 billion has been disbursed so far, of which €6.9 billion as macro-financial assistance, €18.1 billion for defence procurement, and €800 million channelled through the Ukraine Facility, following the satisfactorily completion of reforms. In 2025 , following up on the commitments by G7 leaders and based on a proposal by the Commission, the EU adopted and disbursed a financial assistance package consisting of an exceptional macro-financial assistance (MFA) loan of €18.1 billion . As part of the package, a loan cooperation mechanism is financed by extraordinary revenues stemming from immobilised Russian sovereign assets. On 29 October 2025 the EU-Ukraine Deep and Comprehensive Free Trade Area entered into force. In 2023 , the EU budget enabled €19.5 billion in assistance to Ukraine, including an unprecedented support package of €18 billion for MFA+. Furthermore, the EU mobilised €1 billion for fast recovery, while guarantee agreements were signed with international financial institutions with potential capacity to unlock over €800 million in investments from the Ukrainian private sector for the recovery and reconstruction of the country’s economy. In 2022 , a total of €11.6 billion was provided in loans and grants. These helped Ukraine keep paying wages and pensions, restore critical infrastructure that is destroyed by the war, maintain essential public services, such as hospitals, schools, and housing for relocated people, and ensure overall macroeconomic stability.

noticias.titulo: Invasive plants show limited spread in Andalusia's mountains
noticias.resumen: A study by the University of Córdoba (UCO) departments of Forest Engineering and of Botany, Ecology and Plant Physiology reveals that the presence of invasive plants in Sierra Nevada and the Sierra de los Filabres—two mountain ecosystems in Andalusia that are especially vulnerable to climate change and home to unique plant species—is currently low. Specifically, invasive plants are most common in the areas closest to the edges of roads, and their presence declines at the highest points of the mountains.

noticias.contenido: Country: Ukraine Source: UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights Please refer to the attached file. In Ukraine Civilians Die at Alarming Rates Amid Intensifying Attacks, UN Human Rights Officials Say Kyiv, November 17, 2026 -- Powerful weapons of war kill ever growing numbers of civilians across Ukraine, the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine (HRMMU) said today. Attacks in October alone left at least 372 civilians dead and 1,981 injured HRMMU reported in its monthly update. The report notes that the number of killed and injured in October of this year was 95 per cent higher than in October 2025. The latest figures show that this year has seen significantly higher casualties than previous years. The alarming trend continued in November which saw one of the deadliest single attacks for civilians since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion. On 2 November multiple bombs struck the premises of a school, including an underground shelter in Komyshuvakha in south-eastern Ukraine, where civilians had gathered to receive humanitarian assistance. Ukrainian authorities announced on 16 November that 72 people had died in the attack and that four others were still missing. HRMMU continues to verify the identity and status of those killed, but has already confirmed that dozens of them were civilians, including local residents, local administration staff and emergency workers. "The first ten months of this year have seen more civilian deaths than all of 2025, which in turn was worse than the year before," said Danielle Bell who heads HRMMU. "The world should not become numb to the deadly toll the war exacts on Ukraine's civilians," she said. Long-range weapons (missiles and drones) remain the leading cause of civilian casualties, accounting for more than half of those killed and injured. In October, casualties from aerial glide bombs increased, with the number of civilians killed doubling compared with September, reaching 92 killed and 331 injured. Aerial glide bombs and short-range drones accounted for nearly equal shares of civilian casualties, 18 and 19 per cent, respectively. In October, Russian armed forces significantly intensified attacks on energy infrastructure across Ukraine as the country braces for its fifth winter at war. The attacks damaged electricity and heating infrastructure, temporarily disrupting power and, in some cities, also water supply, forcing Ukrainian authorities to introduce rolling power outages across the country. Ukrainian armed forces also attacked electricity infrastructure in Russian-occupied territory of Ukraine. Meanwhile according to public statements by Russian authorities on individual incidents in October, at least 90 people were killed and 306 injured in occupied territory and at least 59 people were killed and 402 injured in the Russian Federation as a result of Ukrainian attacks, but HRMMU is not able to verify the figures because of lack of access and independent sources of information. In territory of Ukraine occupied by Russia HRMMU verified that at least 12 civilians were killed and 18 injured. In all 17,994 civilians have been killed and 57,854 have been injured in Ukraine since Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February of 2022. Note: HRMMU will publish its findings related to the attack in Komyshuvakha in due course. For media inquiries, please contact Kris Janowski, Spokesperson +380952300437, krzysztof.janowski@un.org

noticias.contenido: Country: Sudan Source: World Health Organization 17 November 2026, Khartoum, Sudan – The World Health Organization (WHO) is calling for sustained support to keep essential health services functioning in Sudan’s White Nile and North Kordofan states, where conflict, displacement, disease outbreaks and shortages of medicines and power continue to strain the health system. The call follows a WHO mission to Kosti in White Nile State, and to El Obeid, North Kordofan’s capital, from 7 to 12 November, led by WHO Representative in Sudan Dr Abdinasir Abubakar. “The health needs I witnessed in White Nile and North Kordofan are immense. We urgently need to scale up essential health services in peripheral localities and displacement camps,” said Dr Abdinasir. “Despite enormous challenges, health workers and partners remain committed to serving the most vulnerable communities. We must match their commitment with sustained support.” Prolonged conflict, displacement, food insecurity, disease outbreaks and malnutrition have severely disrupted health services. Across Sudan, 21 million people need health assistance, while 37% of health facilities are non-functional. The mission highlighted continuing gaps in electricity supplies, medicines, operational resources and access to care in both states. Power interruptions continue to disrupt critical services, including operating theatres, intensive care, neonatal incubators, oxygen generation, blood banks, dialysis and laboratory services, putting patients at risk. Reliable power, including solarization, is urgently needed to sustain lifesaving services. White Nile State hosts more than 216 000 internally displaced people and nearly 455 000 refugees – approximately half of Sudan’s refugee population – placing considerable pressure on already strained health services. In North Kordofan, prolonged conflict, displacement, food insecurity and economic hardship are exacerbating health and nutrition needs. El Obeid hosts most of the over 141 000 internally displaced people in Sheikan locality, further straining already overstretched health services. WHO support to Kosti Teaching Hospital reached more than 24 000 people between November 2025 and April 2026. WHO also supported oxygen-cylinder refills, provided three oxygen concentrators and installed solar capacity in the Emergency Department. A separate solar system at Kosti Renal Dialysis Centre is helping sustain lifesaving emergency dialysis services during frequent power outages. In El Obeid, WHO support in 2025–2026 has contributed to approximately 344 500 health services, including 90 000 patient consultations. WHO also provided over 9000 litres of fuel to help maintain electricity at El Obeid Teaching Hospital, alongside medicines, supplies, capacity-building and operational support. During the mission, Dr Abdinasir met with state government officials, health authorities, WHO teams and humanitarian partners to review priority needs and ongoing humanitarian response and recovery interventions. In Kosti, he opened a training workshop on Ebola virus disease preparedness, and in El Obeid he joined the monthly Health Cluster meeting with six health partners to strengthen coordination and the collective health response. WHO calls for urgent, sustained flexible funding to maintain and expand essential health services, support frontline health workers, strengthen outbreak preparedness and response and ensure reliable medical supplies, power and emergency referral systems. Safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access and the protection of health workers, patients and health facilities are also crucial. WHO continues to work with health authorities, communities, Health Cluster partners and donors to sustain lifesaving services and support the recovery of Sudan’s health system.

noticias.autor: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
noticias.contenido: Country: Côte d'Ivoire Source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Please refer to the attached file. FOOD SECURITY SNAPSHOT Cereal production forecast above average in 2026 Prices of rice near or below year-earlier levels About 1.3 million people severely acute food insecure during 2026 lean season Cereal production forecast above average in 2026 In southern bimodal rainfall areas, harvesting of the 2026 main season maize and rice crops was completed in September. Generally favorable weather conditions between March and July 2026 supported crop establishment and development. However, heavy rains in June and July triggered localized flooding, particularly around Abidjan, damaging crops in some areas. Planting of the secondary-season maize and rice crops was also completed in September. Below-average cumulative precipitation amounts between September and October constrained planting operations and early crop development in several areas. Weather forecasts indicate a high likelihood of above-average rainfall amounts in November across most producing regions, which are expected to improve crop conditions, while increasing the risk of localized flooding. By contrast, below-average precipitation amounts are forecast in some minor producing coastal areas. In northern unimodal rainfall areas, harvesting of the 2026 coarse grain and rice crops is underway and expected to conclude by year-end. The May-October rainy season started on time or up to three weeks earlier than usual in some areas, supporting planting operations and crop establishment. Near-average cumulative rainfall amounts through October were generally conducive to crop development, and production prospects are favorable. Aggregate cereal production in 2026 is preliminarily forecast at about 4.4 million tonnes, approximately 20 percent above the average of the previous five years. The good output mainly reflects an expansion in planted area, officially estimated at 25 percent above average, supported by government programmes providing agricultural inputs and machinery to farmers in collaboration with technical and financial partners. Prices of rice near or below year-earlier levels Prices of locally produced rice, a key staple food, were generally stable between June and September 2026, with seasonal increases of up to 5 percent recorded in some markets. Despite these increases, prices in September were near or up to 10 percent below their year-earlier levels across monitored markets. About 1.3 million people severely acute food insecure during 2026 lean season According to the latest Cadre Harmonisé (CH) analysis, about 1.3 million people (5 percent of the analysed population) were estimated to face severe acute food insecurity (CH Phase 3 [Crisis] and above) during the June-August 2026 lean season, including more than 14 500 people in CH Phase 4 (Emergency). This represents a slight improvement from the same period in 2025, when approximately 1.4 million people (6 percent of the analysed population) were estimated to face CH Phase 3 (Crisis) and above. Spillover effects of the conflict in the Central Sahel remain a major driver of acute food insecurity in northern areas, particularly in the Tchologo and Bounkani regions, where 12 and 14 percent of the analysed population, respectively, were estimated to be in CH Phase 3 (Crisis) and above. These regions host about 85 percent of the country’s 88 000 registered refugees and asylum seekers, while continued arrivals from Burkina Faso and Mali are placing additional pressure on natural resources and livelihoods in host communities. Persistent insecurity in border areas is also restricting access to farmland and pastures and disrupting food supplies to local markets, where elevated prices have been reported. Households’ economic access to food also remains a concern. The guaranteed farmgate price of cocoa, the country’s main export crop, for the 2026/27 main marketing season is 57 percent below the level set at the start of the previous marketing season and is expected to reduce incomes among households dependent on cocoa production. In addition, recent increases in domestic diesel prices, linked to high international oil prices, have raised transport costs and may exert upward pressure on food prices, further constraining households’ purchasing power. Flooding in southern areas affected about 21 500 people in 2026 and caused damage to homes, productive assets, crops and road infrastructure. The resulting disruptions to trade flows and market supplies contributed to localized food price increases.

noticias.contenido: Country: Haiti Source: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification Please refer to the attached file. Vue d’ensemble L’analyse de la situation nutritionnelle révèle une situation précaire sur l’ensemble du territoire avec une prédominance des zones en situation d’Alerte nutritionnelle. Pour la période de juin à novembre 2026, les communes d’Arcahaie, Cabaret et Cité Soleil se trouvent en situation nutritionnelle Sérieuse (Phase 3 de l’IPC), principalement à cause de la situation sécuritaire, de l’insécurité alimentaire persistante et du poids des phénomènes morbides. Par ailleurs, 59 communes sont placées en état d’Alerte nutritionnelle (Phase 2 de l’IPC), tandis que cinq départements et sept communes affichent une situation Acceptable (Phase 1 de l’IPC). Pour la période projetée de décembre 2026 à mai 2027, une nette dégradation de la situation nutritionnelle est attendue en lien avec une dégradation probable des conditions sécuritaires, socio-politiques, épidémiologiques et climatiques. Les communes de Cabaret et Cité Soleil basculeront en situation Critique (Phase 4 de l’IPC), tandis qu’Arcahaie est susceptible de se maintenir en situation Sérieuse (Phase 3 de l’IPC), rejointe par 28 autres communes qui quitteront la phase d’Alerte pour la phase Sérieuse. Parallèlement, les départements des Nippes, du Nord-Est et du Sud-Est, ainsi que cinq communes, passeront de la situation Acceptable à la situation d’Alerte, où se maintiennent déjà 31 autres communes. En revanche, la situation restera Acceptable (Phase 1 de l’IPC) pour les départements du Nord et du Sud, ainsi que pour deux communes du département de l’Ouest. Par ailleurs, sur la période de juin 2026 à mai 2027, plus de 253 700cas de malnutrition aiguë globale (modérée et sévère) sont attendus chez les enfants de 6 à 59 mois. Parmi eux, près de 93 900 enfants risquent de souffrir de malnutrition aiguë sévère, une forme particulièrement critique qui augmente fortement le risque de mortalité. Il est enfin important de noter que l’analyse n’a pas permis d’examiner de manière désagrégée certains groupes particulièrement vulnérables, notamment les personnes déplacées internes (PDI). Une mise à jour plus granulaire apparaît donc nécessaire afin de mieux appréhender leurs vulnérabilités spécifiques et d’orienter plus efficacement les interventions en fonction de leurs besoins. La réalisation rapide d’une enquête nutritionnelle est indispensable pour mesurer l’ampleur de la crise et optimiser le déploiement des interventions d’aide. Partout dans le pays, l’impact direct de la crise sécuritaire avec les déplacements de population et l’insécurité alimentaire persistante, exacerbée par les chocs climatiques et la crise économique, dégrade fortement la situation nutritionnelle. À cela s’ajoutent des déterminants majeurs tels que la forte morbidité infantile (paludisme, diarrhées, infections respiratoires) et les épidémies récurrentes de choléra, ainsi que les carences liées à l’alimentation et aux pratiques de soin (faiblesse de l’allaitement maternel exclusif). La deuxième édition de l’analyse IPC de la malnutrition aiguë (IPC MNA) en Haïti a couvert l’ensemble des 10 départements du pays. L’analyse a été menée à l’échelle départementale pour les Nippes, le Nord, le Nord-Est, le Sud et le Sud-Est, tandis qu’elle s’est faite à l’échelle communale (couvrant 69 communes) pour l’Artibonite, le Centre, la Grand’Anse, l’Ouest et le Nord-Ouest. Les facteurs contributifs à cette situation nutritionnelle précaire varient selon les zones analysées. Dans les zones classées en Phase 3 de l’IPC, les principaux facteurs contributifs sont l’insécurité résiduelle, la précarité de la consommation alimentaire des enfants et l’insécurité alimentaire persistante. S’y ajoutent une forte prévalence des infections respiratoires aiguës et de la fièvre, la faiblesse de la couverture sanitaire ainsi que de mauvaises conditions d’hygiène.

noticias.autor: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
noticias.contenido: Countries: South Sudan, Ethiopia Source: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies Please refer to the attached file. Description of the Event Date when the trigger was met 23-12-2025 What happened, where and when? The Marburg Virus Disease (MVD) outbreak was declared in Ethiopia on 14 November 2025, prompting heightened preparedness measures in neighboring South Sudan due to the risk of cross-border transmission through frequent population movement, trade, and pastoral migration. On 23 December 2025, three suspected MVD-related deaths were reported in Kapoeta East County, including two individuals with a recent travel history to the affected areas of Ethiopia and one suspected community-linked case. These alerts triggered increased preparedness and readiness efforts by the South Sudan Red Cross (SSRC) in collaboration with the Ministry of Health and partners. The operation was implemented from 30 December 2025 to 28 February 2026 in the high-risk border counties of Akobo, Maiwut, Pibor, and Kapoeta East, which had been identified as priority locations because of their proximity to Ethiopia and high levels of cross-border movement. Preparedness activities included volunteer training, community-based surveillance, risk communication and community engagement (RCCE), infection prevention and control (IPC), hygiene promotion, and Safe and Dignified Burial (SDB) preparedness. During implementation, the epidemiological situation remained stable and no confirmed MVD cases were reported in South Sudan. Investigations into suspected alerts, including those reported in Kapoeta East, did not result in any confirmed Marburg cases, and one suspected alert investigated during the operation tested negative. However, operational challenges affected implementation. In Akobo and Maiwut, insecurity and localized conflict restricted access to some communities and required volunteers and staff to relocate temporarily to safer locations while continuing awareness activities where feasible. In Pibor, cattle-raiding incidents disrupted planned interventions and limited access to some target areas. In Kapoeta East, poor road conditions and the remoteness of border communities presented logistical challenges, although SSRC successfully reached border locations, trained volunteers, and implemented preparedness activities. By the end of the operation, no confirmed MVD cases had been detected in South Sudan. The outbreak situation in Ethiopia had improved, transmission had been brought under control, and preparedness capacities in the targeted counties had been strengthened through trained volunteers, community awareness, surveillance systems, IPC measures, and SDB readiness mechanisms.

noticias.titulo: Copilot is "the new OS for work," and now Office runs inside of it

The announcement is a striking inversion of how we've traditionally used software. Rather than an app like Word being the attraction and Clippy the assistant to help you use it, Microsoft envisions the new Copilot integrations will see agents driving things, with the software packages riding shotgun. Applications will become plugin components of the agent's work, backed by an organizational knowledge layer that draws context from emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files. Users will now be able to create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations directly in Copilot, with the resulting files remaining editable in their respective Office applications. noticias.contenido: Country: Afghanistan Source: Save the Children KABUL, 18 November 2026 – More than half of children displaced in Afghanistan said they have less food to eat since leaving their homes, while two in five reported worsening health, according to a new Save the Children report that reveals the severe toll displacement is taking on children across the country. The “Children on the Move” report, based on interviews with more than 800 children and caregivers in seven provinces in Afghanistan, found that displacement over the past three years has deepened hunger, disrupted education and exposed children to heightened protection risks. More than nine in 10 children surveyed had experienced displacement or migration. More than half (55%) of children said they had less food to eat after moving, 41% said their health had deteriorated, and a third (33%) of caregivers said children's access to education had worsened. But despite growing needs, support is failing to reach many children. Fewer than one in 10 children surveyed said they had received any assistance, while nine in 10 said they needed support to access food. The findings come after more than 6.67 million Afghans have returned from Pakistan and Iran since September 2023 – increasing the population by up to 14% - and putting greater pressure on families and communities already struggling with poverty, food insecurity and repeated crises. [2]. Afghanistan also has one of the highest rates of internal displacement globally, with about 7 million people , or around 14% of the population, displaced as of 2025. [3]. Economic hardship is the main driver of displacement in Afghanistan. Nearly half of children (49%) said their families moved because they could not find work or earn enough income, while a third cited food shortages. Almost one in four said their families had relocated due to deportation or pressure to leave another country. Nearly seven out of 10 children surveyed have endured two or more crises in the last three years, including drought, floods, earthquakes and conflict. Compounding crises and displacement are affecting children’s wellbeing in Afghanistan, with children facing growing protection risks. Just over one in 10 (11%) said they had been exposed to at least one protection risk, including child labour, physical or verbal violence or early marriage. Caregivers reported that girls faced particularly high risks during displacement journeys and after arriving in new locations. Among those affected is Nooria*, 8, who arrived in Afghanistan for this first time earlier this year after her family left Pakistan where they had built their lives over five decades. Nooria*, her parents and three siblings arrived with little more than the clothes they carried. Nooria* said: “We returned from Pakistan. We had a home there, and I had many friends. I like Afghanistan too, but I miss my school and my friends. We used to play together and laugh a lot. “We want to have a school like the one we had in Pakistan, where we can continue our education.” Nooria’s family cannot afford the transport costs to send her to school, but she attends classes at a Save the Children temporary learning space. Her mother, Nazoo*, 28, said: “My husband does not have a job here, and we have no source of income to provide for our children's needs. I worry every day about how we will find food for our next meal. “When you are born in a country and get married there, that place becomes your home. You feel that you belong there. When you suddenly have to leave, your whole life falls apart, especially when you arrive with nothing.” The ‘Children on the Move’ report found that assistance reaching children is extremely limited, with significant gaps between needs and the support they receive. Ashish Damle, Country Director, Save the Children in Afghanistan said: “No child should have to abandon their homes, schools and communities for safety or survival - but for many, displacement has become part of their childhood. Children face dangerous journeys with serious protection risks, only to arrive in places where their families are still struggling to put food on the table, access healthcare and send them to school. “Our ‘Children on the Move’ research reveals a deeply concerning reality - finding a new home does not mean reaching safety. Girls and children with disabilities in particular face greater protection risks, while poverty is forcing families to make impossible choices just to survive, often with little or no humanitarian assistance. “Children who have already lost their homes should not be left to face these risks alone. We urgently need sustained funding to protect them along migration routes and ensure they can access essential services wherever they settle. “These children deserve more than day to day survival. They deserve the chance to feel safe, return to school and rebuild their lives.” Save the Children has been working in Afghanistan since 1976, including through periods of conflict, displacement and natural disasters. We currently run programmes in nine provinces and work with partners across an additional 11 provinces, delivering services in health, nutrition, education, child protection, shelter, water, sanitation, hygiene and livelihoods. References: Multimedia content: https://www.contenthubsavethechildren.org/Package/2O4M1TH4VWH9 * Denotes name changed to protect identity [1] Key findings: https://resourcecentre.savethechildren.net/document/children-on-the-move-research-study-afghanistan-2026 . Save the Children’s ‘Children on the Move’ study in Afghanistan was conducted in selected locations affected by floods, droughts, earthquakes, and conflict, identified as migration source, transit, and destination areas. The primary study population was children on the move aged 0–17 years and their families. 824 children and 838 caregivers were interviewed through structured questionnaires and 32 qualitative consultations conducted with key informants and caregiver groups in July 2026. The study covered seven provinces; Nangarhar, Herat, Balkh, Faryab, Kabul, Kandahar and Sar-e-Pul. The findings are representative of Save the Children operational areas covered by the study, not of Afghanistan as a whole. [2] Number of returnees as of 31 October 2026 from UN and partners. Population increase calculation using UN population figure of 48.6m https://www.unocha.org/afghanistan [3] https://www.internal-displacement.org/database/displacement-data/ For interview requests and further information, please contact: Rachel Thompson, Media Manager, Asia: Rachel.thompson@savethechildren.org Our media out of hours contact is media@savethechildren.org.uk / +44(0)7831 650409

noticias.titulo: EU advances Syrian recovery and reconstruction through Syria Partnership Coordination Forum in Damascus
noticias.resumen: Country: Syrian Arab Republic Source: European Commission Please refer to the attached file. Today, the Syria Partnership Coordination Forum (SPCF) convened in Damascus for the first time to advance Syria's recovery and reconstruction, showcase investment opportunities and agree on concrete steps forward. The SPCF brought together key partners, including EU Member States, the G7, Arab countries, and the UN and International Financial Institutions, such as the World Bank, the European Investment Bank, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the Islamic Development Bank, as…
noticias.contenido: Country: Syrian Arab Republic Source: European Commission Please refer to the attached file. Today, the Syria Partnership Coordination Forum (SPCF) convened in Damascus for the first time to advance Syria's recovery and reconstruction, showcase investment opportunities and agree on concrete steps forward. The SPCF brought together key partners, including EU Member States, the G7, Arab countries, and the UN and International Financial Institutions, such as the World Bank, the European Investment Bank, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the Islamic Development Bank, as well as civil society, to discuss Syria's business environment and steps to translate Syria's priorities into concrete investment opportunities. The Forum, co-chaired by Syria and the EU, was opened by Commissioner for the Mediterranean Dubravka Šuica and the Syrian Minister of Foreign Affairs, Assaad Al-Shaibani. Economic revitalisation, institutional recovery and improved livelihoods In her second visit to the country, Commissioner Šuica officially launched the Syria Technical Assistance Hub to support Syrian institutions in strengthening their capacities and advancing reforms that are instrumental to restore confidence, attract responsible investment and support sustainable economic recovery. The Commissioner also witnessed the signing of new EU-funded contracts supporting Syria's recovery and reconstruction, namely on the rule of law, on an enabling business environment andon support to small and medium-sized enterprises . These initiatives will help revive the economy, strengthen public institutions and improve livelihoods. By helping businesses access finance and grow, the projects can create jobs and improve conditions for investment. They will also improve access to justice, supporting a recovery that benefits people across Syria. During her bilateral meeting with Minister Al-Shaibani, Commissioner Šuica received Syria's signed undertaking to implement the EU's Registered Exporter system . This marks an important step towards enabling Syrian products to benefit from preferential access to the EU market under the Generalised Scheme of Preferences, opening up new opportunities for Syrian exporters and supporting the country's economic recovery. Commissioner Šuica also visited the Deir Ali Power Plant together with Ibrahim Al-Adhan, Syrian Deputy Minister of Energy and EIB Vice President Gelsomina Vigliotti. The visit highlighted the importance of restoring Syria's energy infrastructure for economic recovery and explored opportunities for future EU engagement in the energy sector with other international partners. Background After the fall of the Assad regime at the end of December 2024 and following the Brussels IX Conference of 17 March 2025, Syria and the EU launched the SPCF, which provides a platform to align partners' support on Syria's recovery priorities and coordinate on their implementation. The Forum is instrumental in facilitating structured engagement among key partners, including EU Member States, the G7, Arab nations, and International Financial Institutions. The SPCF is structured under regular senior-official plenary meetings at capital level, and regular practical level. It builds on the EU's support for Syria's recovery. During her first visit to Damascus in June 2025, Commissioner Šuica announced €175 million to help Syria rebuild its institutions, advance transitional justice and revive its economy. In January 2026, President Ursula von der Leyen announced around €620 million in EU support for 2026–2027 to support recovery and provide humanitarian aid. In May 2026, the Council restored the full application of the EU–Syria Cooperation Agreement, paving the way for stronger trade ties. On 16 November 2026, EU Foreign Ministers supported moving ahead with the EU-Syria Association Agreement. In December, a Day of Dialogue will take place for the second time in Damascus, organised by the Syrian authorities, Syrian civil society and the EU. It will provide a platform for inclusive dialogue on Syria's transition and the role of civil society. For more information EU support to Syria - factsheet The EU announces €175 million to support recovery in Syria EU opens new chapter in its relations with Syria Quote(s) A peaceful, stable and inclusive Syria is important for Syrians, to the region and to Europe. The EU is ready to deepen its partnership with Syria as Syrians rebuild their country for all citizens. At today’s Forum in Damascus, we focused on what international partners and businesses can do to support the country’s own priorities, so people can find jobs, businesses can reopen and services can further be restored. noticias.titulo: Rare encounter with isolated Indigenous Awá people in Brazil exposes vulnerability
noticias.resumen: On Nov. 16, a group of roughly 20 Indigenous Awá people living in voluntary isolation approached an Indigenous Guajajara village, in Brazil’s northeastern Maranhão state. The rare encounter has mobilized Indigenous peoples and activists concerned about the safety of the Awá, considered the most threatened group on the planet. The motivation for the unusual interaction […]
noticias.contenido: On Nov. 16, a group of roughly 20 Indigenous Awá people living in voluntary isolation approached an Indigenous Guajajara village, in Brazil’s northeastern Maranhão state. The rare encounter has mobilized Indigenous peoples and activists concerned about the safety of the Awá, considered the most threatened group on the planet. The motivation for the unusual interaction is unclear, but Guajajara leaders “expressed concern about the physical condition of some members of the group, especially children and older people, who appeared to be very thin,” according to accounts and images posted on social media by Indigenous organizations. The Guajajara reportedly offered the Awá food and other objects; the Awá remained there briefly before returning to the forest. Brazil’s Indigenous affairs agency, Funai, told Mongabay by email that technical teams are monitoring the situation and that it had activated a contingency plan to “ensure that the relevant agencies are prepared to respond appropriately to any developments in the situation, especially regarding the ethno-environmental protection, health and safety of the Indigenous people involved.” Funai added that the peoples’ right to self-determination would continue to be respected. Unlike other isolated peoples who make frequent contact, this is the first time in decades that the Awá of the Arariboia Indigenous Territory “have appeared in this way and made such close contact with other people,” Sarah Shenker, director and senior researcher at the Indigenous rights organization Survival International Brazil, told Mongabay by phone. noticias.titulo: Turning food waste into insect feed poses only low mad cow disease risk
noticias.resumen: Insects can convert food waste and by-products from the food industry (such as unsold ready meals or slaughter by-products) into ingredients for animal feed. In this way, they can contribute to the transition toward a circular food production system, in which what would otherwise be wasted is reused. However, these waste streams may contain animal proteins that pose a risk of transmitting diseases such as bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), also known as mad cow disease. For this reason, rearing insects on waste streams containing animal proteins is not permitted in the European Union.

noticias.titulo: Yet another satellite company is jockeying for a rocket—but this one makes sense
noticias.resumen: "Governments need control of their critical space infrastructure, and Europe needs it most."
noticias.contenido: Finnish satellite developer ICEYE announced Tuesday that it is seeking to buy Italian rocket-maker Avio for more than $2.2 billion in a transaction aimed at creating Europe's first true vertically integrated end-to-end space company. The announcement came as an all-cash voluntary tender offer from an Italian subsidiary of ICEYE to Avio's shareholders, led by the Italian defense conglomerate Leonardo. Avio said its board of directors "has taken note of the notice" from ICEYE and is considering the purchase offer. Avio builds the Vega C rocket, a solid-fueled launcher designed to carry up to 3.3 metric tons (7,300 pounds) of payload to low-Earth orbit. The Vega C has flown successfully seven times in eight attempts since 2022. It is a follow-on to an earlier version of the Vega rocket that amassed a 20-for-22 record since debuting in 2012. noticias.resumen: From tracking how cancer develops to exploring how the brain works, scientists need ways to observe biological processes at increasingly smaller scales. The tool integrates four ecological objectives: reducing species extinction risk, prioritizing carbon stocks, restoring riparian areas and assessing ecological feasibility. The findings show that including ecological feasibility changes restoration priorities, while 80.4% of the selected areas contribute to more than one ecological objective. By identifying areas where different priorities overlap…
noticias.contenido: Researchers from Chile's Institute of Ecology and Biodiversity (IEB) have developed a multiobjective model to identify priority areas for large-scale ecological restoration in Chile, South America. The tool integrates four ecological objectives: reducing species extinction risk, prioritizing carbon stocks, restoring riparian areas and assessing ecological feasibility. The findings show that including ecological feasibility changes restoration priorities, while 80.4% of the selected areas contribute to more than one ecological objective. By identifying areas where different priorities overlap, the model can help guide strategic restoration planning and support better-informed conservation decisions amid growing environmental challenges and limited resources.

noticias.titulo: Hundreds of websites deliver potent malware cocktail to unsuspecting visitors
noticias.resumen: Malware cocktail delivers cryptocurrency theft payloads and iOS exploits, among other things.
noticias.contenido: Hundreds of websites using the Optimizely website personalization platform served unsuspecting visitors a potent malware cocktail that targeted cryptocurrency wallets, stole payment card data, cookies, and screenshots, and delivered exploit kits for infecting iPhones and iPads, researchers said Tuesday. ReportURI said it identified 178 websites—including CNN, Zoom, the BBC, and Salesforce—that were affected. JavaScript digitally signed by Optimizely and then loaded into customer pages had been modified to include malicious components that attempted to infect visitor devices with multiple payloads. When wares were installed successfully, they swapped user cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the attackers. Other components skimmed payment cards, stole cookies and screenshots, and, on iPhones and iPads, delivered iOS exploit kits known as Coruna and DarkSword. Optimizely infrastructure delivers multipurpose malware Optimizely serves JavaScript “snippets” that include both company code and code that is provided by each customer. The JavaScript, which can be served directly from Optimizely or from a customer endpoint, runs on every page the customer serves. Somehow, the attackers wrote their own code into a portion of each affected customer’s JavaScript and then delivered it from cdn.optimizely.com. A valid certificate for that domain signed the JavaScript. Read full article Comments

noticias.titulo: Bird flu wiped out the Sandwich tern colony in 2022, three years later, 756 of them have returned
noticias.resumen: After suffering from High Pathogenic Avian Influenza in 2022, the Sandwich tern colony at Pagham Harbour faced severe population loss. Through extensive conservation efforts, the colony saw a remarkable recovery, breeding 756 pairs by 2026. This comeback has also benefited other bird species, such as black-headed gulls and avocets. RSPB rangers and volunteers have played a crucial role in habitat management and safety.

noticias.titulo: Polémica en Uruguay: suspenden a dos docentes que insultaron a alumnos en una clase virtual
noticias.resumen: La Universidad Tecnológica reprobó las declaraciones de los profesores y les inició sumarios administrativos
noticias.contenido: Dos docentes de la Universidad Tecnológica de Uruguay fueron sumariados y suspendidos por insultar a alumnos durante una clase virtual. El episodio ocurrió después de que se difundiera en redes sociales una videollamada privada entre docentes de la Licenciatura en Tecnologías de la Información , en la que realizaron comentarios despectivos y profirieron insultos contra estudiantes de la institución. A lo largo de la conversación, además, dieron a entender que el encuentro había sido convocado como un espacio de consulta para los alumnos previo a un evaluación, aunque ninguno se presentó. Los docentes no se dieron cuenta que la clase estaba siendo grabada. Suspenden a dos docentes que insultaron a alumnos En uno de los pasajes de la grabación, uno de los docentes afirma: “No van a venir. Los voy a mandar a todos a examen. Que se vayan todos a la puta que los que lo parió, me tienen harta” . “Esto no pasa a defensa, a no ser que cambien mucho con todas las correcciones que les hice, que les hice un libro a cada uno . Poco más diciéndole: ‘Usted es bobo, haga esto’. No podés defender algo que está mal”, señala en el video que se viralizó. La grabación también incluye referencias a estudiantes de cursos anteriores. En ese contexto, la profesora menciona el caso de un alumno que, según relata, había recursado la asignatura varias veces y protagonizado un conflicto luego de que no le permitieran acceder a la instancia de defensa de su trabajo final. “ Qué gente pelotuda, gente grande. Él era un psicópata, recusante de recursantes” , agrega la docente. Su colega responde: “Trabajé con él. Qué tipo pedante ese ”. En determinado momento, los docentes advierten que la sesión estaba siendo grabada automáticamente y la profesora comenta que eliminará ese fragmento. “Yo elimino esto, lo elimino del calendar” , se la escucha decir. La grabación concluye instantes después con otra frase de la profesora: “Bueno, seguiré corrigiendo estas porquerías de entrega”. La reacción de la facultad La difusión del video provocó una rápida reacción de las autoridades universitarias. A través de un comunicado el Consejo Directivo Central de la UTEC manifestó su repudio a las expresiones formuladas por los docentes y remarcó que resultan incompatibles con los valores institucionales. “A partir del conocimiento de un registro audiovisual en el que dos docentes de la Licenciatura en Tecnologías de la Información de la Universidad Tecnológica (UTEC) se refieren a estudiantes en términos incompatibles con los principios de respeto y buen trato que deben regir en la convivencia universitaria, el Consejo Directivo Central manifiesta su rechazo a dichas expresiones”, señalaron en un comunicado que reprodujo El País de Uruguay. “ El respeto y el buen trato son principios fundamentales de nuestra comunidad universitaria . En este sentido, UTEC reafirma su compromiso con el bienestar de sus estudiantes y con la construcción de un entorno educativo en el que todas las personas se sientan valoradas y respetadas”, añadieron. En ese sentido, el Consejo dispuso “la instrucción de sumarios administrativos a ambos docentes, así como su suspensión preventiva mientras se desarrollan los procedimientos correspondientes”. “La universidad reafirma su compromiso con una convivencia basada en el respeto mutuo y en los valores que deben orientar el relacionamiento entre todos los integrantes de su comunidad”, concluyó la UTEC.

noticias.titulo: NASA Launches Nuclear Power Systems Student Contest
noticias.resumen: NASA’s Power to Explore Student Challenge kicked off Tuesday, Nov. 17. The science, engineering, technology, and mathematics (STEM) challenge invites kindergarten through 12th grade students in the United States to learn about space nuclear power systems and illustrate how these nuclear “batteries” could help power their lunar exploration vision. Students are also invited to write […]
noticias.contenido: The thematics for the 2026-2027 Radioisotope Power Systems Power to Explore Student Challenge Credit: NASA / David Lam NASA’s Power to Explore Student Challenge kicked off Tuesday, Nov. 17. The science, engineering, technology, and mathematics (STEM) challenge invites kindergarten through 12th grade students in the United States to learn about space nuclear power systems and illustrate how these nuclear “batteries” could help power their lunar exploration vision. Students are also invited to write a short essay about a “superpower” of their own. Submissions are due March 1, 2027. Every mission requires a power source. Some of the most interesting locations to study on our Moon face some of the harshest conditions. Nuclear power could sustain human life and allow researchers to study the resource-rich environment despite freezing temperatures, long nights, and deep craters that never see sunlight. “As NASA returns to the Moon and establishes a lunar base where astronauts will live, work, and explore, we need to build an infrastructure to make it all possible. Nuclear power could enable exploration in the permanently shadowed regions near the Moon’s South Pole, carry robust science payloads over long distances, and keep instruments warm through the lunar night,” said Carl Sandifer, a program manager for NASA’s Space Reactors Division at the agency’s headquarters in Washington. “NASA’s Power to Explore Student Challenge prepares the next generation of explorers to use the unique power within themselves to dream up a nuclear-powered Moon base of their own design. We cannot wait to see what they come up with!” Entries include a 200-word essay and an original illustration. Essays should describe one of the students’ unique powers that will help the mission. Illustrations should convey the students’ vision of a nuclear-powered lunar base that supports human and robotic exploration of the Moon’s surface using both radioisotope and fission-based power solutions and demonstrate the students’ understanding of the kinds of exploration nuclear energy can enable. Judges will review entries in three grade-level categories: K-4, 5-8, and 9-12. One grand prize winner from each grade category will receive a trip for two to NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland to learn about the people and technologies that enable NASA missions. Every student who submits an entry will receive a digital certificate and an invitation to a virtual event with NASA experts where they’ll learn about what energizes the NASA workforce to advance NASA’s missions and sustain America’s leadership in space. Judges Needed NASA and Future Engineers are seeking volunteers to help judge the thousands of contest entries anticipated from around the country. U.S. residents older than 18 who are interested in volunteering approximately three hours should register to judge at the Future Engineers website . The Power to Explore Student Challenge is funded by the NASA Science Mission Directorate and operates out of the Radioisotope Power Systems Program under the Research and Technology Mission Directorate. Future Engineers administers the challenge through a contract with the NASA Center of Excellence for Collaborative Innovation within the agency’s Research and Technology Mission Directorate. To learn more about the challenge, visit: https://www.nasa.gov/power-to-explore Eighteen-year-old Thomas Lui of Ridgewood, New Jersey; nine-year-old Rainie Lin of Lexington, Kentucky; and twelve-year-old Aadya Karthik of Seattle, Washington, winners of the 2024 Power to Explore Student Challenge explore an Apollo capsule at NASA Glenn’s Visitor Center at the Great Lakes Science Center, as a part of their prize trip to Cleveland. Photo Credit: NASA / Dave Lam

noticias.titulo: Jason Clay, who persuaded big business to help save nature, has died at 75
noticias.resumen: In 1988 Jason Clay attended a Grateful Dead concert at Madison Square Garden and met a man who wanted to help save tropical rainforests. Clay, an anthropologist who had worked with Indigenous communities, asked what he did for a living. “I make ice cream,” the man replied. It was Ben Cohen of Ben & Jerry’s. […]
noticias.contenido: In 1988 Jason Clay attended a Grateful Dead concert at Madison Square Garden and met a man who wanted to help save tropical rainforests. Clay, an anthropologist who had worked with Indigenous communities, asked what he did for a living. “I make ice cream,” the man replied. It was Ben Cohen of Ben & Jerry’s. Clay suggested developing a flavor using nuts gathered from tropical forests. He thought higher payments for forest products might give people a reason to keep the trees standing. Within a year, Rainforest Crunch was on supermarket shelves. Clay set up a trading company and went on to work with more than 50 businesses on some 200 products, generating roughly $100 million in retail sales. At one point, he said, his operation was buying around a fifth of the world’s Brazil nuts. It paid gatherers two or three times the going rate, and other buyers raised their prices to compete. The people gathering the nuts weren’t generally the ones clearing the forests. Ranchers and loggers had little reason to change what they were doing, and Clay eventually called Rainforest Crunch a failure. “We were attacking the wrong driver,” he explained in a 2010 TED talk. He should have been working on beef, lumber and soy. Clay, who died on November 16th aged 75, spent more than three decades at the World Wildlife Fund (WWF), where he worked to change how major companies bought agricultural commodities linked to deforestation and other environmental problems. noticias.titulo: Fin de fiesta para Lula: el dólar se dispara, los mercados tiemblan y hasta sus aliados hablan de “estafa electoral” por el ajuste
noticias.resumen: Los inversores consideran que el paquete de recortes enviado al Congreso es modesto y cortoplacista; lo ven insuficiente para contener la creciente deuda pública
noticias.contenido: BRASILIA.– Lula da Silva ni siquiera comenzó su cuarto mandato y ya enfrenta su primera prueba de fuego. Tres semanas después de vencer en el balotaje al senador Flavio Bolsonaro, el presidente volvió el lunes a Brasilia, tras una gira por Asia y Europa, y encontró un mercado en pleno tembladeral. Tras saltar 2,15% ese mismo día, el dólar llegó este martes a tocar los 5,81 reales, su valor más alto desde abril de 2025, y cerró a 5,78, con una suba mínima del 0,08%, mientras la Bolsa de San Pablo ensayaba un leve rebote después de caer 1,83% en la víspera. El contexto externo no ayuda -la caída de las tecnológicas en Wall Street y las apuestas a subas de tasas en Estados Unidos-, pero el foco está en Brasilia. La disparada del lunes “fue un fenómeno brasileño, que no acompañaron las monedas de otros países emergentes”, afirmó Milton Maluhy, CEO de Itaú Unibanco, el mayor banco privado del país, en un foro de la federación de bancos. Y lanzó una advertencia: si no se hace nada, la deuda pública podría superar el 100% del PBI al final del cuarto mandato de Lula. Por detrás del sacudón en el mercado, los inversores consideran tímido el primer paquete de ajuste fiscal que el gobierno envió al Congreso la semana pasada y esperan definiciones clave, empezando por quién conducirá el Ministerio de Hacienda en el nuevo mandato del líder del Partido de los Trabajadores (PT). Desde el balotaje del 25 de octubre, el Ibovespa, principal índice de la bolsa de San Pablo, acumula una pérdida de cerca de 18% y el dólar subió más de 16%. Morgan Stanley rebajó su recomendación para las acciones brasileñas a “venta” y advirtió sobre un riesgo “relevante” de dominancia fiscal, es decir, que la deuda pese tanto que las subas de tasas dejen de contener la inflación y el dólar. El paquete, bautizado “plan Moretti” en referencia al ministro de Planificación, Bruno Moretti, prevé un impacto de hasta 60.000 millones de reales -poco más de 10 mil millones de dólares- en el presupuesto de 2027, combinando un freno al crecimiento del gasto, recortes de exenciones tributarias y la postergación de transferencias a estados y municipios. Pero el mercado calcula un ahorro más modesto. XP Investimentos estima los efectos permanentes en unos 38.300 millones, y su equipo macroeconómico concluyó en un informe que el paquete está “excesivamente volcado al corto plazo” y no reduce la dinámica de la deuda en los próximos años. El Senado aprobó el texto base el jueves pasado por un ajustado 45 a 31 y debía votar este martes cuatro modificaciones presentadas por la oposición. El gobierno apostaba por un “supermartes”. Según el ministro de Relaciones Institucionales, José Guimarães, existía acuerdo con el presidente de la Cámara de Diputados, Hugo Motta, para votar el proyecto este mismo día, apenas llegara del Senado. Pero, pese a la expectativa del gobierno, la votación se postergó para el miércoles, ante la falta de acuerdo entre los senadores sobre qué modificaciones aprobar o rechazar. “Estamos muy preocupados por esta suba del dólar y la perspectiva de tasas altas”, dijo Motta, que pidió al gobierno “construir otras salidas” además de este ajuste. Rebelión en las bases Sin embargo, otro ruido relevante para Lula vino de la propia base, algo que muestra la encerrona que enfrenta. Desde el ala más a la izquierda del PT, figuras como el diputado Lindbergh Farias acusaron al equipo económico de apartarse de un programa de campaña que no mencionaba recortes. Hubo quienes hablaron de “estelionato electoral” (estafa electoral) estafa electoral y de “tijeretazo”, el término que ministros de Lula y el diputado André Janones usaron en las redes durante la campaña contra las propuestas de ajuste de Flavio Bolsonaro. Las críticas fueron luego contenidas -la bancada petista expresó su apoyo-, pero Guimarães debió salir a explicar que en el oficialismo “no hay crisis”, sino “divergencias, como siempre en la izquierda”. En ausencia de Lula, le tocó al vicepresidente Geraldo Alckmin el lunes salir a calmar los ánimos: “No hay razón para que el mercado tenga estas oscilaciones. Creo que serán pasajeras”. El ministro de Hacienda, Dario Durigan, definió el paquete como apenas “el primer paso” de un proceso gradual. “El único camino es un ajuste gradual, que respete el gasto social, pero sin negacionismo sobre la necesidad de mejorar las cuentas”, dijo. Lula tomó este martes la articulación de su administración en sus manos. Desde temprano recibió en el Palacio de la Alvorada a Alckmin, a Moretti, a la jefa de la Casa Civil, Miriam Belchior, y a líderes parlamentarios, y tenía prevista una reunión para retomar las conversaciones sobre la formación del gobierno con tres de sus principales colaboradores de campaña: el senador Camilo Santana, mencionado para la Casa Civil; el senador electo Rui Costa, y el gobernador de Piauí, Rafael Fonteles. La otra gran incógnita es el gabinete. Lula se prepara para definir antes de fin de mes quién estará al frente de Hacienda. Entre los nombres que circulan figuran el propio Alckmin, Fonteles y la continuidad de Durigan, que gana fuerza por su papel en el paquete. El reparto de cargos para partidos del denominado “centrão” será otra prueba. El presidente del PT, Edinho Silva, pidió a sus senadores que exijan garantías de voto antes de llevar pedidos de cargos al Planalto. Hay urgencia. El Congreso que asumirá en febrero será aún más conservador, con el Partido Liberal de Bolsonaro como primera fuerza en el Senado y en Diputados. El desafío de Lula es doble. El presidente debe dar señales que calmen al mercado sin alimentar las acusaciones de “estelionato electoral” que llegan desde su propia base. Por eso, el gobierno salió a negar recortes en áreas sensibles como salud y educación –Moretti prometió que el presupuesto sanitario crecerá en 2027-, aunque el proyecto elaborado por su equipo retira, por caso, ingresos extraordinarios del petróleo de la base de cálculo de los pisos constitucionales de ambos sectores.

noticias.titulo: NASA Space Apps Challenge Breaks Global Hackathon Records
noticias.resumen: On Nov. 14 and 15, NASA held the annual Space Apps Challenge with a record-breaking 181,835 registered participants taking part in 593 events around the world. The annual hackathon invites participants to use NASA’s open data to address one of 14 challenges focused on space exploration or Earth science. This year, the hackathon drew 59% […]
noticias.contenido: 2 min read NASA Space Apps Challenge Breaks Global Hackathon Records Two NASA Space Apps Challenge participants in Vilhena, Brazil work together during the annual hackathon on their project submission. NASA On Nov. 14 and 15, NASA held the annual Space Apps Challenge with a record-breaking 181,835 registered participants taking part in 593 events around the world. The annual hackathon invites participants to use NASA’s open data to address one of 14 challenges focused on space exploration or Earth science. This year, the hackathon drew 59% more registrants and was the 5th year in a row with increased participation. Since 2012, NASA Space Apps Challenge has hosted the two-day event, which has included more than 600,000 people from more than 190 countries. The challenge provides an opportunity for hands-on experience with NASA science, mobilizing an engaged global community of technologists and space science enthusiasts to answer questions that benefit humanity and drive exploration. Participants join events organized by local volunteers to work in teams and address one of the challenges and submit their project before the deadline. Projects are then judged to determine 10 global winners, to be announced in January. “The Space Apps Challenge invites people with many different skillsets to leverage NASA’s gold-standard datasets to address real challenges facing us here on Earth and in space,” said Amy Kaminski, engagement branch chief, Science Mission Directorate, NASA Headquarters in Washington. “We’re thrilled to see more than 180,000 people tackling these challenges and helping to accelerate our ability to find solutions.” One of the local winning teams from NASA Space Apps Challenge NYC pose with volunteer local lead Nate Cooper. NASA Challenges also feature data from 17 international space agency partners, all Artemis Accord signatories. This year’s space agency partners are: Angola National Space Programme Management Office (GGPEN), Bahrain Space Agency, Brazilian Space Agency (AEB), CSA (Canadian Space Agency), ESA (European Space Agency), ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation), Italian Space Agency, JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency), KASA (Korea AeroSpace Administration), Mohammed Bin Rashid Space Center of the United Arab Emirates, National Space Activities Commission of Argentina (CONAE), Nigeria’s National Space Research and Development Agency, Paraguayan Space Agency, Senegalese Space Studies Agency, Spanish Space Agency, Turkish Space Agency, and UK Space Agency. Three agencies, GGPEN, AEB, and CONAE, also wrote challenges this year. noticias.titulo: Nvidia supera expectativas y gana 59.335 millones en su tercer trimestre, un 105% más
noticias.resumen: Nvidia, el gigante de los chips que ha posibilitado el 'boom' de la inteligencia artificial , ha presentado resultados muy positivos para el tercer trimestre. La compañía batió su récord de ingresos en esos tres meses, con 115.800 millones de dólares de ingresos, más del doble que el mismo periodo de hace un año y por encima de las expectativas de Wall Street . Los analistas pronosticaban unos ingresos en el entorno de los 100.000 millones.Nvidia también superó las expectativas del mercado en cuanto a beneficios, que llegaron a 65.300 millones de dólares para ese trimestre.Los resultados…
noticias.contenido: El fabricante estadounidense de microprocesadores avanzados Nvidia logró un beneficio neto de 65.287 millones de dólares (unos 59.335 millones de euros) en su tercer trimestre fiscal, comprendido entre finales de julio y finales de octubre, lo que supone elevar sus ganancias en un 105% respecto al año anterior y superar los pronosticos de los analistas, en sus primeras cuentas trimestrales con Jensen Huang fuera de la directiva tras saltar el escándalo relacionado con sus infidelidades. De su lado, los ingresos de la firma alcanzaron los 115.844 millones de dólares (105.282 millones de euros), un incremento del 103% en comparación a hace doce meses. Las acciones de Nvidia cerraron prácticamente planas en los 155,46 dólares (-0,48%) este martes previo a la presentación de resultados, en una jornada marcada además por el anuncio de declaración de Huang ante el Congreso de Estados Unidos y ante la declaración de intenciones del recién dimitido CEO sobre su voluntad de volver al cargo. Sin embargo, los títulos de la compañía ha llegado a repuntar hasta un 3,5% en el mercado 'after hours' una vez desveladas las cuentas trimestrales que ha superado las previsiones de los mercados.

noticias.titulo: EE.UU. atacó una base de misiles iraní en la isla Qeshm en represalia por los ataques a Bahréin
noticias.resumen: Un funcionario norteamericano confirmó el bombardeo de una instalación militar en la isla, en el estrecho de Ormuz
noticias.contenido: TEHERÁN.– Estados Unidos atacó este martes una base iraní de misiles en la isla de Qeshm , en el estrecho de Ormuz, según confirmó un funcionario estadounidense. La operación se conoció después de que Teherán denunciara explosiones en ese territorio y en medio de un nuevo repunte de los ataques entre ambos países, cuyos enfrentamientos habían disminuido desde septiembre. La agencia oficial iraní reportó “cinco o seis explosiones” en Qeshm. El vicegobernador provincial afirmó que no hubo daños. Washington no había confirmado inicialmente el bombardeo; luego, un funcionario estadounidense informó que aviones de combate norteamericanos atacaron una base de misiles en la isla. Estados Unidos ya había atacado Qeshm a principios de noviembre, en una operación que describió como “limitada” y “defensiva” . Tercer ataque iraní contra Bahréin El bombardeo de Qeshm ocurrió después de que Irán lanzara drones contra una instalación de radar estadounidense en Bahréin , el tercer ataque contra objetivos militares norteamericanos en cinco días. Los Guardianes de la Revolución dijeron que apuntaron contra un radar en la base aérea de Sheikh Isa, como respuesta a las “repetidas violaciones” del espacio aéreo iraní por drones estadounidenses. Las autoridades de Bahréin afirmaron que sus defensas aéreas interceptaron el ataque . El ejército estadounidense sostuvo que no hubo daños en sus equipos ni heridos entre sus efectivos. Los ataques anteriores ocurrieron el viernes y el domingo: Teherán reivindicó impactos contra radares estadounidenses, pero Washington y Manama aseguraron que los drones fueron derribados o interceptados. Bahréin alberga la 5ta Flota de la Armada de Estados Unidos , una de las principales bases navales norteamericanas. Esa presencia lo convierte en un objetivo estratégico para Irán. El bloqueo y la presión sobre Teherán La guerra comenzó el 28 de febrero , con bombardeos de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán. Después de una etapa de enfrentamientos más intensos, el conflicto se concentró en el estrecho de Ormuz, por donde suele circular cerca de una quinta parte del suministro mundial de petróleo y gas. La navegación continúa gravemente obstaculizada. Estados Unidos mantiene desde hace meses un bloqueo naval sobre Irán que limita sus exportaciones de crudo y presiona su economía. A la vez, protege a los buques tanque que transportan petróleo desde los países árabes del Golfo, lo que permitió que los envíos regionales regresaran a niveles cercanos a los anteriores a la guerra. Washington reforzó además su presencia militar: el portaaviones USS Theodore Roosevelt se sumó al USS George H.W. Bush y al USS George Washington. Los analistas ven en los ataques contra Bahréin una posible modificación de la estrategia iraní. Mostafa Najafi sostuvo que Teherán podría haber pasado de responder a las ofensivas a tomar la iniciativa. Hamidreza Azizi, del International Crisis Group, planteó que los dirigentes iraníes deben determinar si intentar romper el bloqueo mediante una escalada resulta menos costoso que aceptar su continuidad. Las negociaciones siguen estancadas, pese a los esfuerzos de mediación de Qatar. Doha pidió moderación y advirtió que una nueva escalada pone en peligro las posibilidades de un acuerdo. Egipto, Arabia Saudita y Emiratos Árabes Unidos también condenaron los ataques iraníes contra Bahréin. La tensión se extendió a las rutas comerciales . La agencia británica UKMTO recibió un reporte sobre un ataque contra un buque tanque al norte de Omán; el segundo impacto habría provocado un incendio. También informó que un carguero frente a Yemen repelió un intento de abordaje. La agencia iraní Fars afirmó que dos barcos chocaron con minas en Ormuz, aunque no estaba claro si se trataba de los mismos incidentes. La inteligencia estadounidense reportó sobre presuntos planes iraníes para un ataque con una bomba sucia contra Washington . Araqchi lo negó y lo calificó de propaganda; Trump dijo que se toma “muy en serio” esa posibilidad. No se presentaron pruebas sobre ese plan. Agencias Reuters, AP y AFP
